comparisons.peer_topic: All Other Segment Managed Basis Presentation
comparisons.peer_summary: All Other results are presented on a managed basis excluding divestiture-related impacts to provide transparency, improve peer comparison, and support strategic views.
comparisons.comparison: While JPMorgan presents segment results on a 'managed basis' generally, Citigroup specifically presents 'All Other' results on a managed basis that excludes divestiture-related impacts. Both companies utilize a 'managed basis' presentation to provide transparency into operational performance, though Citi applies this exclusion specifically to certain segments to aid peer comparison and strategic views.

sentences.text: Segment results are presented on a managed basis.

All Other results are presented on a managed basis that excludes divestiture-related impacts related to (i) Citi's divestitures of its Asia consumer banking businesses and (ii) the planned IPO of Mexico Consumer/SBMM within All Other-Legacy Franchises.

The managed basis presents investors with a view of operating earnings that provides increased transparency and clarity into the operational results of Citi's performance; improves the visibility of management decisions and their impacts on operational performance; enables better comparison to peer companies; and allows Citi to provide a long-term strategic view of the business going forward.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and composition of business segments
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm manages and reports its activities in three business segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management, and Platform Solutions, which are organized based on products, services, customers, and counterparties.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs define their business segments based on the products and services provided or the types of customers served, reflecting the internal management structure. JPMorgan states that segments reflect the manner of evaluation by its Operating Committee, while Goldman Sachs explicitly states its segments are organized based on these factors and are reported as such.

sentences.text: The business segments are determined based on the products and services provided, or the type of customer served, and they reflect the manner in which financial information is evaluated by the Firm's Operating Committee, whose members act collectively as the Firm's CODM.
These business segments are determined and organized based on products and services provided, and the types of customers and counterparties served.

comparisons.peer_topic: Chief Operating Decision Maker and performance metrics
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's president and chief operating officer serves as the chief operating decision maker (CODM), who allocates resources and assesses segment performance principally based on total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders, and return on average common equity.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify a specific body or individual acting as the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) that evaluates segment performance. JPMorgan identifies its Operating Committee (collectively) as the CODM, whereas Goldman Sachs identifies its President and Chief Operating Officer as the CODM. Both use this role to allocate resources and assess performance.

sentences.text: The business segments are determined based on the products and services provided, or the type of customer served, and they reflect the manner in which financial information is evaluated by the Firm's Operating Committee, whose members act collectively as the Firm's CODM.
The firm's chief operating decision maker (CODM) is its president and chief operating officer.

The CODM makes operating decisions, assesses the performance of, and allocates resources to, the firm's operating segments principally based on the total net revenues of the segments, revenues net of provision for credit losses, total operating expenses, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders and the return on average common equity to assess the performance of the segments.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm structures its business segments based on the nature of financial products and services provided, aligning with the assessment method used by the chief operating decision maker (CODM).
comparisons.comparison: Similar to JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley structures its segments based on the nature of financial products and services provided, aligning this structure with the approach used by its CODM to assess financial performance. JPMorgan also aligns its segment determination with how financial information is evaluated by its CODM.

sentences.text: The business segments are determined based on the products and services provided, or the type of customer served, and they reflect the manner in which financial information is evaluated by the Firm's Operating Committee, whose members act collectively as the Firm's CODM.

The Firm structures its segments primarily based upon the nature of the financial products and services provided to customers and its management organization, which is consistent with the approach used by the Firm's chief operating decision maker ("CODM") to assess the Firm's financial performance.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Chief Executive Officer serves as the CODM, evaluating segment performance and allocating resources based on business, strategic, and financial considerations including income before taxes, pre-tax margin, and return on average common equity.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley disclose the identity of their CODM in the context of segment reporting. JPMorgan identifies the Operating Committee, while Morgan Stanley identifies its Chief Executive Officer, as the entity responsible for evaluating segment performance and allocating resources.
